# Resend — transactional email for Next.js Resend sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) through a small HTTP API with delivery logs, webhooks and domain verification. The official Node.js library `resend` wraps the whole Resend REST API, has typed responses and works in Node.js 18+, serverless and edge runtimes. ## Install ```bash npm install resend ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` RESEND_API_KEY=re_placeholder RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The API key is created in the Resend dashboard (API Keys). The From address must be on a domain you have verified in Resend, or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/resend.ts`: ```ts import { Resend } from "resend"; export const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the API key to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Welcome!", html: "

Thanks for signing up.

", text: "Thanks for signing up.", }); ``` `data.id` is the message id; use it to look the email up in the dashboard logs. ## 4. Send with a React template Write the email as a React component and pass it with `react`; Resend renders it to HTML: ```tsx import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; import { PasswordResetEmail } from "@/emails/password-reset"; await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Reset your password", react: PasswordResetEmail({ name: "Ada", actionUrl: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }), }); ``` The `@react-email/components` package gives layout primitives for email clients; plain JSX works too. ## 5. Handle errors `emails.send` does not throw on a refused message: it resolves to `{ data: null, error }` with the error `name` and `message` from Resend (invalid API key, unverified domain, rate limit). Check `error` where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Resend - Built for developers: one API call to send, typed SDK, React templates in the codebase. - Delivery logs, bounces and webhooks live in the same dashboard as the API keys. - Domain verification with DKIM and SPF guided from the dashboard. # Postmark — transactional email for Next.js Postmark sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) with high delivery rates, bounce and spam processing, and detailed statistics. The official Node.js library `postmark` covers the whole Postmark REST API, uses the native Fetch API and has no runtime dependencies (Node 18+). ## Install ```bash npm install postmark ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN=server_token_placeholder POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The server token belongs to one Postmark server (Servers → API Tokens). The From address must be a confirmed sender signature or sit on a verified domain. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/postmark.ts`: ```ts import { ServerClient } from "postmark"; export const postmark = new ServerClient(process.env.POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the server token to the browser. ## 3. Send an email # Notely A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind. ## Status - Users live in `src/lib/users.ts` as an in-memory list. - `/dashboard` shows the current user and the team. - There is no sign-in, no billing, and no email yet. ## Develop ```bash npm run dev ``` src/app/favicon.ico src/app/layout.tsx src/app/page.tsx src/app/globals.css src/lib/users.ts src/app/dashboard/page.tsx

content.text:
Welcome and password-reset emails are now wired into `src/lib/users.ts`, sent through Resend. I haven't sent a real email, since there's no API key here. Lint passes and my files typecheck. `tsc` still reports one error in `src/app/layout.tsx` (`LayoutProps` not found), which I didn't touch.

I picked Resend because its docs in `docs/` cover a plain server-side call with no template tooling, and a small app doesn't need more.

- **`src/lib/email.ts` (new):**
  - It holds a lazy Resend client plus `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`, with HTML and plain-text bodies and the user's name escaped.
  - A failed or refused send is logged and never thrown, so an email problem can't break signup.
  - If the credentials aren't set, it logs a warning and skips the send, which keeps dev working without a key.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:**
  - There was no user-creation or reset code, so I added `createUser`, `requestPasswordReset` and `consumePasswordResetToken`.
  - `createUser` lowercases the email, rejects duplicates and sends the welcome email.
  - `requestPasswordReset` creates a random one-hour token and stores only its hash. It returns the same result whether or not the email exists, so it can't be used to check which emails have accounts.
  - `consumePasswordResetToken` checks the token and makes it single-use.
  - Like the existing user list, the reset tokens are in-memory and are lost on restart.
- **`.env.example`:** `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` and `APP_URL`, all placeholders. The repo's `.gitignore` excludes `.env*`, so you'll need `git add -f .env.example`.
- **`package.json` and README:** `resend` is added as a dependency, and the README status line now mentions email.

The reset email links to `/reset-password?token=…`, but that page doesn't exist yet, and neither does anything that calls `createUser` or `requestPasswordReset`. You need a sign-up and a forgot-password route, a reset page, and password storage. None of those exist because the app has no sign-in yet.

I haven't committed anything.
